name: Massachusetts

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt.
Alcohol bought in stores: beer, wine and spirits bought in stores are exempt from sales tax (taxed instead by a wholesale excise, by volume); drinks served in restaurants and bars are taxed as meals.
Cigarettes are taxed at 6.25%, on top of the $3.51-a-pack excise (since 2013), left out here; other tobacco and vapor products carry wholesale excises.
Household supplies: diapers are exempt, which is not taken out here.
Personal care products: tampons, sanitary napkins and incontinence pants are exempt, which is not taken out here.
Barber and beauty services: haircuts and other personal services aren't taxed.

Clothing and footwear are exempt up to $175 an item. Jewelry and watches are taxed at 6.25% and counted on their share of US sales of clothing, shoes and jewelry (13%, 2022 Economic Census), 0.81% of what is spent on clothing, shoes and jewelry; the category's rate also takes in laundry and dry cleaning, at their own rate. Also taxed but not counted, since no official figure gives their share: the part of an item's price over $175, other accessories such as handbags, and athletic uniforms and protective wear. The August 8 and 9, 2026 sales tax holiday also exempted single items of $2,500 or less, jewelry and the part of clothing over $175 included.
Laundry and dry cleaning are services and aren't taxed.
Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and taxed by the gallon instead (24 cents for gasoline since 2013), left out here.
Auto repair labor: car repair labor is not taxed; parts are, itemized on the bill.
No local sales taxes apart from the local meals excise.

Hotel stays pay the 5.7% state room occupancy excise plus local options (up to 6%, 6.5% in Boston, a 2.75% convention center fee in Boston, Cambridge, Chicopee, Springfield, West Springfield and Worcester, and 2.75% in Barnstable County towns for the Cape Cod and Islands Water Protection Fund), which are not counted here.

Cities and towns may add a local excise of up to 3% on marijuana sales, not counted here; Question 8 on the November 3, 2026 ballot proposed repealing adult-use sales and this excise; its result has not been read yet.
Personal and professional services, haircuts and car repair labor among them, are not taxed; parts and products sold with them are (DOR guide).
gaps: Massachusetts has no local general sales tax; the 6.25% state rate applies everywhere.
272 of the 351 cities and towns have adopted the local option meals excise (0.75%) on restaurant meals, counted in their restaurant rate here.

Cities and towns are county subdivisions, many of them not Census places, so the meals excise is given for each adopting town (272 in all): a census tract shared by towns counts each town's excise for the share of the tract's jobs at restaurants, bars and hotels located in it (LEHD LODES jobs by census block; residents where the tract has none), since the tax is charged where meals are bought.
The state also taxes restaurant meals at 6.25%; local room-occupancy and cannabis excises are not included.

programs: MassDevelopment's Transformative Development Initiative districts are mapped where active (seven, in the fourth cohort; graduated districts aren't shown), and the multifamily districts of MBTA Communities that comply with the zoning law (MassGIS), and Worcester's 11 Commercial Area Revitalization Districts (M.G.L. c. 40D; the city's layer, April 2025). Boston's Downtown business improvement district is mapped as of 2018; the Greenway district (approved in 2019) is drawn only on a 2017 layer, so it isn't shown, and the state keeps no list of the others. Economic Target Areas, Massachusetts Downtown Initiative areas, District Improvement Financing and Urban Center Housing TIF districts, Housing Development Zones and the Mass Cultural Council's cultural districts have no statewide map. The 26 Gateway Cities on the state's list (unchanged since 2013–14, as reported) are named on their pages, with the cities that, as reported, have left or met the law's criteria since.
